analysis.session_summary: The tape was dictated by Iran Strait headlines: an early proposal to reopen the Strait produced a sharp risk-on/JPY-down impulse, then later Trump comments urging negotiation and economic isolation reversed much of the move. The day closed with the USD bid (DXY +0.237%), safe havens JPY and CHF firm, while EUR and GBP were weakest (currency strength -0.155 and -0.163). Brent/USD still closed +0.655% and VIX fell -2.803% with SPX +0.152%, so the risk tone was not one-way. Most majors closed near session lows/highs in the direction of late USD strength.

themes.evidence: The 10:30 Iran proposal to reopen the Strait triggered an 86.7-pip USD/JPY drop, 30.5-pip EUR/USD rally, 31.7-pip GBP/USD bounce and 1402.7-pip USD/ZAR drop; later Trump isolation headlines helped reverse those legs.

themes.theme: USD and safe-haven resilience against EUR/GBP
themes.evidence: DXY +0.237%, currency strength USD +0.168, JPY +0.138, CHF +0.103 vs EUR -0.155 and GBP -0.163; EUR/USD -32.3 pips, GBP/USD -38.7 pips, USD/CHF +4.6, USD/JPY +4.5.

themes.theme: High-beta FX and oil complex remain headline-sensitive
themes.evidence: USD/SEK +266 pips, USD/MXN +744.1 pips, USD/ZAR -168.4 pips on close while Brent/USD +0.655%; intraday legs in USD/SEK, USD/NOK, USD/ZAR and USD/MXN whipsawed around Iran headlines.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD whipsawed from 15.2 pips up to 40.3 down, then 30.5 up on Iran relief and 30.8 down on Trump isolation, ending -32.3 pips near session lows.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD mirrored EUR/USD: 16.1 up, 47.7 down, 31.7 up, 39.9 down to close -38.7 pips.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY produced the biggest swing: 48.3 up, 86.7 down on Iran proposal, 58.4 recovery, closing only +4.5 pips but with a 94.5-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF left a 41.0-pip range as risk-off bid and Iran relief flowed through, ending +4.6 pips.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD chopped through multiple legs, including 23.1 up after RBA Bullock and 23.0 up on Iran relief, but faded to -17.7 pips.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD had a 54.3-pip range with 47.0 up, 26.5 up on Iran and late -26.6 down, closing nearly flat at +0.7 pips.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD grinded higher after early dip, with a 41.1-pip late leg, closing +39.4 pips near the high.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF slid 30.3 pips over 1050 minutes then recovered only 10.0 pips to close -21.3.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY was extremely whippy with 84.8 up, 88.8 down and 53.3 up legs, ending -7.3 pips in a 103.1-pip range.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD fell 100.8 pips in the center leg and rebounded 35.8 to close -32.5 pips, consistent with NZD strength.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP held a very tight 14.6-pip range across six small legs, ending +0.7 pips.
leg_notes.USD/SEK: USD/SEK whipsawed from -239.0 to +508.7 then -614.3 and +612.3, closing +266 pips.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN mirrored risk headlines with 758.6 up, 489.8 down, 704.0 up, closing +744.1 pips.

scenarios.name: USD resilience / Trump isolation keeps risk premium
scenarios.thesis: The late Trump comments urging Iran isolation keep USD/JPY bid and risk-high-beta under pressure, extending the day's USD resilience; EUR/GBP remain soft into PMIs.
scenarios.invalidation: Concrete Strait de-escalation or strong EUR/GBP PMIs break the USD bid and high-beta recovers.

pair_paths.rationale: Measured 40.3-pip downside leg from 06:45 to 10:15 can extend if USD resilience persists.
May replicate measured 47.7-pip selloff into London if UK PMI softens.
Measured 58.4-pip recovery after Iran relief shows late USD bid if isolation rhetoric continues.
Measured 41.1-pip late up-leg supports extension with oil risk.
Late 26.6-pip NZD/USD decline can continue if USD strength dominates.

scenarios.name: Concrete de-escalation / Iran Strait reopening follow-through
scenarios.thesis: If Iran opening becomes concrete, the 10:30 risk-on pattern returns: JPY and USD lose as oil drops, high-beta and commodity FX recover.
scenarios.invalidation: Another US isolation announcement or no follow-through reverses risk-on.

pair_paths.rationale: Matches 86.7-pip drop on the initial Iran proposal.
Matches 31.7-pip relief rally on Iran proposal.
Matches 26.5-pip NZD/USD up-leg on Iran proposal.

scenarios.name: Rangebound consolidation after headline exhaustion
scenarios.thesis: Market digests PMIs and holds within today's ranges; no fresh catalyst extends USD strength or reversal.
triggers: PMIs in line (German mfg 54.1, services 49.9; UK mfg 51.5, services 52.0)
scenarios.invalidation: A large PMI surprise or fresh Iran headline breaks today's ranges.

risks.why_it_matters: The initial Iran proposal caused an 86.7-pip USD/JPY drop and a 30.5-pip EUR/USD rally; later Trump isolation headlines reversed these moves, so any new headline can re-whip the tape.
risks.watch: High-level meeting reports and any Strait reopening confirmation.

risks.why_it_matters: EUR and GBP are the weakest majors on the day (-0.155 and -0.163) and the coming flash PMIs can extend those moves if they miss the 50/consensus levels.
risks.watch: French, German, UK flash manufacturing and services PMIs.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The next window brings French, German and UK flash PMIs; with EUR/GBP already weak and prints near neutral, misses could extend the USD bid, while any concrete Iran de-escalation remains the larger swing factor.
